correctness.rationale: PASS: The symmetric-sector diagonal-unique-continuation induction uses all nonzero adjacent couplings and arbitrary diagonal terms cancel at already-zero amplitudes. Any invariant collision-dark symmetric subspace would contain a forbidden H eigenvector. Dissipativity puts every symmetric K eigenvalue strictly below the real axis, and Jordan bounds yield exponential conditional convergence. The product rule follows from the antisymmetric projector identity. Reproducibility includes 48 seeded complex-hopping/disordered-interaction tests, 144 states, spectral dark-space counts and the four-cycle boundary; these checks corroborate rather than replace the proof. Risks: no uniform decay rate in n or near vanishing rates; graph/path and complete monitoring assumptions essential.

value.rationale: PASS: Complete diagonal observability (dimension n(n+1)/2) in the symmetric square of arbitrary weighted Jacobi matrices gives a structural, all-parameter answer to collision-loss robustness. This distinguishes zero residual loss (bosonic symmetric sector) from exactly conserved loss-free fermionic sector independently of site disorder, interactions and losses, and gives universal survival for any mixed preparation. The four-cycle supplies a mathematically motivated geometric boundary. It is more than a special numerical case, normalization identity, or a restatement of the previously known two-site mechanism.
